headline: The Right Order: Wall Tile Before Floor Tile in Your Bathroom?
articleBody:
When you're planning a bathroom renovation, one common question that pops up is about the order of operations, especially for tiling. Should you install the wall tile first, or the floor tile? It might seem like a small detail, but getting the sequence right can actually save you a lot of headaches and ensure a much cleaner, more professional finish.

The general consensus among experts, and what we typically follow at HH Remodeling LLC, is to install your bathroom wall tile *before* the floor tile. This isn't just a random preference; there are some solid reasons behind it. First, working on the walls before the floor means any drops of thinset, grout, or stray pieces of tile will fall onto your subfloor, which is much easier to clean up or will be covered by the new floor anyway. If you did the floor first, you'd constantly be worried about damaging or dirtying your pristine new floor tiles during the wall installation process.

Secondly, installing wall tile first helps with the alignment and junctions. It allows for a cleaner transition where the wall tile meets the floor, as the wall tile can extend down to meet the un-tiled floor. This can make the perimeter of the room look much more integrated. It also minimizes the risk of damaging your newly laid floor tiles when you're moving ladders or tools around to reach higher wall sections. Once the wall tiles are set and cured (which usually takes about 24 hours before grouting), then you can confidently move on to the floor.
